   197	
   198	Checks two scalar steps in the lower bound obtained from restarted time

1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels refer to the manuscript
     6	revision 3920258 and are written exactly as in its LaTeX source (for
     7	example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written and reviewed
     8	at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9 and ba01d98. The later revisions
     9	changed only prose, titles, the literature review, layout and figures:
    10	every cited label exists in all four, and the mathematical expressions of
    11	each cited statement and its proof are the same up to whitespace and braces
    12	(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    13	
    14	## Scope
    15	
    16	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    17	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    18	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`; `Audit/<module>/` prints the
    19	  elaborated types.
    20	- The rows cover every public theorem (470) and 87 definitions whose
    21	  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other
    22	  49 public definitions (for example
    23	  `kappa`, `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`) only name quantities used in those
    24	  statements and have no rows of their own; read their bodies in the Lean
    25	  source or in `Audit/`.
    26	- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
    27	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    28	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
    29	  inner-product and finite-word facts.
    30	- The nineteen `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules (sections marked
    31	  "whole result" below; four of them are the wave-kernel and
    32	  time-fractional foundation of `ClockCopy`) model `H:homog` and formalize
    33	  the conclusions of fifteen
    34	  labelled results in full. Eleven need no supplied input:
    35	  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own
    36	  hypotheses. `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are
    37	  proved under weaker hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no
    38	  `delta < 1`) and also stated exactly as the manuscript does by the
    39	  wrappers `gram_scalar_algebra_paper` and `rayleigh_tail_paper`; the
    40	  Rayleigh lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is
    41	  not formalized. `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters` are proved from the
    42	  numerical part of `H:homog` (a generalization) and also restated under
    43	  the full hypothesis `H:homog`, which `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`
    44	  models clause by clause (covariance measure, spectral measure, evenness,
    45	  temperedness, positive-definiteness, scaling, parameter ranges).
    46	  `L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` and `L:temporal-equilibrium` are stated with
    47	  the manuscript's own hypotheses (`gamma_beta_paper`,
    48	  `temporal_equilibrium_paper`). The finite slice of `S:compact-gaussian`,
    49	  `L:gaussian-trace-bounds`, `P:finite-gaussian-matrix` and
    50	  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`, is stated with the manuscript's
    51	  hypotheses (independent standard Gaussians on an arbitrary probability
    52	  space) on top of a finite Gaussian integration-by-parts foundation
    53	  (`GaussianIBP`). `L:variational-control-dilation` is
    54	  stated with the section's hypotheses (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a =
    55	  alpha0`) by `variational_control_dilation_paper`, for the cost in its
    56	  integral form and the rate defined by the real Rayleigh supremum
    57	  `E:variational-real-rayleigh` (over a weak-gradient `H^1(R^d)` built in
    58	  `WeakSobolev`, since Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces); the identifications
    59	  with `E W(Psi)^2` and `sqrt(-E_s)` are not formalized. Four further results are formalized with
    60	  every conclusion proved but with analytic inputs supplied as named
    61	  hypotheses: `P:radius-mean-anchor` (the moment bound of
    62	  `C:radius-covariance-residuals`, and measurability of the Holder norm of
    63	  the stopped paths) and `L:masked-trig-products` (membership in the
    64	  temporal completion, `L:masked-time-completion`, and the modulation
    65	  bound `L:masked-temporal-modulation`) and `L:raw-block-indexed-cone`
    66	  (the ground family of `S:compact-mean-family`, one hypothesis structure)
    67	  and `P:clock-copy-obstruction` (the homogeneity of the spectral measure,
    68	  which the TeX derives in the proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`; the
    69	  finiteness part of that lemma is also formalized);
    70	  their abstractions are explained
    71	  in their sections. Side conditions the TeX leaves implicit (a probability
    72	  measure, integrability, measurability) are explicit hypotheses, and
    73	  integrability is part of each integral conclusion.
    74	- The SPDE itself, stochastic integrals, Gaussian measures (beyond finitely
    75	  many independent standard Gaussians, `GaussianIBP`), Fourier analysis,
    76	  infinite-dimensional spectral analysis and operator theory (beyond the
    77	  finite-matrix results of `FiniteGaussianMatrix`) and all limits in time or in a
    78	  regularization are outside Lean. Where a Lean statement needs an analytic
    79	  fact about the model, that fact enters as an explicit hypothesis of the
    80	  theorem (a "supplied hypothesis" below). Lean checks the deduction from
    81	  those hypotheses, not the hypotheses themselves.
    82	- A successful `lake build` is not a verification receipt for the
    83	  manuscript. It shows that the stated Lean theorems are proved from their
    84	  hypotheses; whether a statement matches the manuscript step it is listed
    85	  against is a separate, human judgment recorded in this ledger.
    86	- Three further modules developed alongside these (normalized Gaussian
    87	  coordinates, vector Gaussian projection, and colored vector words) are
    88	  withheld from this package because they depend on a library that is not
    89	  yet public.
    90	- "no direct label" means the declaration checks a computation from the
    91	  development of the manuscript that does not appear as, or inside, a
    92	  labeled statement of the revision cited above, or is a Lean-only
    93	  auxiliary or example (such as a non-vacuity instance) with no
    94	  counterpart in the manuscript. Such rows make no claim about the
    95	  manuscript.

1472	## VariationalDilation (whole result)
  1473	
  1474	Formalizes Lemma `L:variational-control-dilation` (Radon and Rayleigh
  1475	dilation; `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` lines 225-268 at
  1476	`3920258`) together with the definitions it uses, in two modules:
  1477	`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WeakSobolev.lean` (a hand-built real Sobolev
  1478	space and the real Rayleigh value set) and
  1479	`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalDilation.lean` (the control class,
  1480	the dilation, the mean, variance, rate and integrated rate, and the lemma).
  1481	The wrapper `variational_control_dilation_paper` states the lemma with the
  1482	section's standing hypotheses (line 4: a nonzero covariance satisfying
  1483	`H:homog`, modelled by `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`, with `a = alpha0`):
  1484	for `r > 0`, `D_r` is a bijection of the class with inverse `D_(1/r)`, and the
  1485	four identities of `E:variational-dilation-values` hold. Nothing is supplied as
  1486	a hypothesis.
  1487	
  1488	Abstractions and why they are faithful.
  1489	The class `E:variational-positive-class` (lines 5-10) consists of smooth
  1490	functions on `R x R^d` with compact support inside `(0,1) x R^d`, i.e. elements
  1491	of `C_c^infinity((0,1) x R^d)` extended by zero. `CPos_nonempty` proves that
  1492	the class is nonempty (lines 13-17) using a different bump. The mean
  1493	`h_{Psi,s}` and the variance `v_Psi` are the
  1494	displays `E:compact-raw-mean` and `E:compact-raw-cost`
  1495	(`notes/integrated_compact_mean_family.tex` lines 402-412), with
  1496	`(Gamma * phi)(x) = int phi(x-y) Gamma(dy)` and `int_0^1` taken over
  1497	`Ioo 0 1`. Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces, so `WeakSobolev` defines
  1498	`H^1(R^d; R)` by weak gradients (`int f d_v phi = -int <g,v> phi` for every
  1499	test function `phi` and direction `v`). It proves that an `L^2` weak gradient
  1500	is unique a.e. (`weakGradient_ae_unique`), so a Rayleigh set built from pairs
  1501	`(f, g)` is the manuscript's set of `f`.
  1502	
  1503	The rate `lambda_{Psi,s}` is defined in Lean by the real Rayleigh form
  1504	`E:variational-real-rayleigh`: `rate = sqrt(sSup R_s)`, where `R_s` is the set
  1505	of values `int h_s f^2 - ||grad f||_2^2` over unit `f in H^1(R^d; R)`. The
  1506	manuscript's primary definition is `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)`, with `E_s` the
  1507	spectral bottom of the self-adjoint `-Delta - h_s` on `H^2`. The manuscript
  1508	proves that the two agree (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`), but that equality is
  1509	**not formalized**, because it needs unbounded self-adjoint operators and
  1510	spectral theory. Likewise `v_Psi` is the integral form of
  1511	`E:compact-raw-cost`, and its identification with `E W(Psi)^2`
  1512	(`L:compact-raw-profile`, which needs the Gaussian noise) is **not
  1513	formalized**. The TeX proof itself works with exactly these two forms
  1514	(Lebesgue substitution in the pairing, and the real Rayleigh bijection).
  1515	
  1516	Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
  1517	- A Rayleigh trial must have `h_s f^2` integrable. For the manuscript's `h_s`
  1518	  this is automatic, because `h_s` is bounded (`L:variational-global-mean`,
  1519	  not formalized). The condition keeps Lean's junk value `0` for a
  1520	  non-integrable integral out of the set.
  1521	- `Psi` is continuous; this follows from smoothness.
  1522	- The identities hold for every real `s`, not only for `s in [0,1]`.
  1523	
  1524	Junk values. Every identity is an exact identity of Bochner integrals and of
  1525	`sSup`. It would remain true if an integrand were not integrable, or if the
  1526	Rayleigh set were empty or unbounded (Lean's value `0` on both sides). The
  1527	companion does not exclude these junk cases. It proves only conditional
  1528	transfers, in `variational_control_dilation_integrable_paper`:
  1529	- every integrand in the definitions of `h`, `v` and `I` is integrable for
  1530	  `D_r Psi` exactly when it is for `Psi`;
  1531	- the Rayleigh sets themselves scale, so a Rayleigh set is nonempty and
  1532	  bounded above for `D_r Psi` exactly when it is for `Psi`.
  1533	
  1534	So if a quantity is a genuine integral or supremum for `Psi`, the identity
  1535	relates it to a genuine integral or supremum for `D_r Psi`. That any of these
  1536	integrands is integrable, or that any Rayleigh set is nonempty and bounded
  1537	above, is **not proved** in Lean: it rests on the finiteness of `v_Psi`
  1538	(`L:compact-raw-profile`), the boundedness of `h_s`
  1539	(`L:variational-global-mean`) and the finiteness of `I_Psi`
  1540	(`P:variational-unmasked-rate`), none of which is formalized. The
  1541	integrability equivalences are Lean-route auxiliaries: the TeX proof
  1542	(lines 243-250) works with nonnegative integrands and Tonelli and states none
  1543	of them. Their rows below say so.
  1544	
  1545	The TeX's square-root step uses positivity of the rates. Lean instead uses
  1546	`sqrt(sSup(r^2 S)) = r sqrt(sSup S)`, which holds for every set `S`.
  1547	
  1548	Hypotheses carried but unused: `Gamma != 0`, and every clause of `H:homog`
  1549	except the set scaling. The general theorems assume only the set scaling
  1550	`SetScaling` and continuity of `Psi`.
  1551	
  1552	Not formalized:
  1553	- `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)` and its positivity (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`);
  1554	- `v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2`, with finiteness and positivity
  1555	  (`L:compact-raw-profile`);

   104	`ℝ × ℝ^d` centred at `(1/2, 0)` with outer radius `1/4` replaces the
   105	manuscript's explicit product of `e^{-1/(1-z²)}` bumps). -/
   106	theorem CPos_nonempty (d : ℕ) : (CPos d).Nonempty := by
   107	  let b : ContDiffBump ((1 / 2 : ℝ), (0 : Rd d)) := ⟨1 / 8, 1 / 4, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩
   108	  refine ⟨b, b.contDiff, b.hasCompactSupport, ?_, fun p => b.nonneg, ?_⟩
   109	  · rw [b.tsupport_eq]
   110	    intro p hp
   111	    refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, Set.mem_univ _⟩
   112	    · have h1 : dist p.1 (1 / 2) ≤ 1 / 4 :=
   113	        (le_max_left _ _).trans (Prod.dist_eq.symm.trans_le (Metric.mem_closedBall.mp hp))
   114	      have := (abs_le.mp (Real.dist_eq _ _ ▸ h1)).1
   115	      show (0 : ℝ) < p.1
   116	      change (-(1 / 4 : ℝ)) ≤ p.1 - 1 / 2 at this
   117	      linarith
   118	    · have h1 : dist p.1 (1 / 2) ≤ 1 / 4 :=
   119	        (le_max_left _ _).trans (Prod.dist_eq.symm.trans_le (Metric.mem_closedBall.mp hp))
   120	      have := (abs_le.mp (Real.dist_eq _ _ ▸ h1)).2
   121	      linarith
   122	  · intro h
   123	    have := congrFun h ((1 / 2 : ℝ), (0 : Rd d))
   124	    rw [b.one_of_mem_closedBall (Metric.mem_closedBall_self (by norm_num))] at this
   125	    exact one_ne_zero this

   127	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the spatial dilation of `ℝ × ℝ^d` as a
   128	homeomorphism. -/
   129	def dilHomeo {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) : ℝ × Rd d ≃ₜ ℝ × Rd d :=
   130	  (Homeomorph.refl ℝ).prodCongr (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r hr)
   131	
   132	/-- `D_r` maps `CPos` into `CPos` for `r > 0`. -/
   133	theorem dil_mapsTo (alpha : ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   134	    Set.MapsTo (dil (d := d) alpha r) (CPos d) (CPos d) := by
   135	  rintro Ψ ⟨hs, hc, ht, hn, hne⟩
   136	  have hL : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun p : ℝ × Rd d => (p.1, r • p.2)) :=
   137	    contDiff_fst.prodMk (contDiff_snd.const_smul r)
   138	  have hcomp : (fun p : ℝ × Rd d => Ψ (p.1, r • p.2)) = Ψ ∘ (dilHomeo hr.ne') := rfl
   139	  refine ⟨contDiff_const.mul (hs.comp hL), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   140	  · have := hc.comp_homeomorph (dilHomeo hr.ne')
   141	    rw [← hcomp] at this
   142	    exact this.mul_left (f := fun _ => r ^ ((d : ℝ) + 2 - alpha))
   143	  · have hsub : tsupport (dil alpha r Ψ) ⊆ (dilHomeo hr.ne') ⁻¹' tsupport Ψ := by
   144	      refine closure_minimal ?_ ((isClosed_tsupport Ψ).preimage (dilHomeo hr.ne').continuous)
   145	      intro p hp
   146	      refine subset_tsupport Ψ ?_
   147	      intro h0
   148	      have e : (p.1, r • p.2) = dilHomeo hr.ne' p := rfl
   149	      exact hp (show r ^ ((d : ℝ) + 2 - alpha) * Ψ (p.1, r • p.2) = 0 by rw [e, h0, mul_zero])
   150	    intro p hp
   151	    have := ht (hsub hp)
   152	    exact ⟨this.1, Set.mem_univ _⟩
   153	  · intro p
   154	    exact mul_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hr.le _) (hn _)
   155	  · intro h
   156	    apply hne
   157	    funext p
   158	    have := congrFun h (p.1, r⁻¹ • p.2)
   159	    simp only [dil, smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_smul, Pi.zero_apply] at this
   160	    exact (mul_eq_zero.mp this).resolve_left (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hr _).ne'
   161	
   162	/-- `D_{1/r} ∘ D_r = id` on all functions, for `r > 0`. -/
   163	theorem dil_inv_dil (alpha : ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) :
   164	    dil alpha (1 / r) (dil alpha r Ψ) = Ψ := by
   165	  funext p
   166	  simp only [dil, smul_smul, one_div, ← mul_assoc]
   167	  rw [mul_inv_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_smul, ← Real.mul_rpow (inv_pos.mpr hr).le hr.le,
   168	    inv_mul_cancel₀ hr.ne', Real.one_rpow, one_mul]
   169	
   170	/-- `D_r ∘ D_{1/r} = id` on all functions, for `r > 0`. -/
   171	theorem dil_dil_inv (alpha : ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) :
   172	    dil alpha r (dil alpha (1 / r) Ψ) = Ψ := by
   173	  have := dil_inv_dil (d := d) alpha (one_div_pos.mpr hr) Ψ
   174	  rwa [one_div_one_div] at this
   175	
   176	/-- First claim of `L:variational-control-dilation`: for `r > 0`, `D_r` is a
   177	bijection of `CPos` with inverse `D_{1/r}`. -/
   178	theorem dil_bijOn (alpha : ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   179	    Set.InvOn (dil alpha (1 / r)) (dil alpha r) (CPos d) (CPos d) ∧
   180	      Set.BijOn (dil (d := d) alpha r) (CPos d) (CPos d) := by
   181	  have hinv : Set.InvOn (dil alpha (1 / r)) (dil alpha r) (CPos d) (CPos d) :=
   182	    ⟨fun Ψ _ => dil_inv_dil alpha hr Ψ, fun Ψ _ => dil_dil_inv alpha hr Ψ⟩
   183	  exact ⟨hinv, hinv.bijOn (dil_mapsTo alpha hr) (dil_mapsTo alpha (one_div_pos.mpr hr))⟩

   185	/-! ### The Radon pushforward of `Γ` -/
   186	
   187	/-- The set-scaling field of `H:homog`, `Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`. -/
   188	def SetScaling (alpha : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
   189	  ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
   190	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
   191	
   192	/-- The pushforward of `Γ` under `y ↦ r y` is `r^{α-d} Γ` (TeX lines 250-251). -/
   193	theorem map_dilation {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   194	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   195	    Γ.map (fun y => r • y) = ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ (alpha - d)) • Γ := by
   196	  ext A hA
   197	  rw [Measure.map_apply (measurable_const_smul r) hA, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
   198	  have : (fun y : Rd d => r • y) ⁻¹' A = r⁻¹ • A := by
   199	    have h := Set.preimage_smul_inv₀ (inv_ne_zero hr.ne') A
   200	    simpa using h
   201	  rw [this, hΓ A hA r⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr hr)]
   202	  congr 2
   203	  rw [Real.inv_rpow hr.le, ← Real.rpow_neg hr.le]
   204	  ring_nf
   205	
   206	/-- `∫ G(r y) Γ(dy) = r^{α-d} ∫ G dΓ` (TeX lines 246-248) for continuous `G`
   207	(unconditional as an identity of Bochner integrals). -/
   208	theorem integral_dilation {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   209	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (G : Rd d → ℝ) (hG : Continuous G) :
   210	    ∫ y, G (r • y) ∂Γ = r ^ (alpha - d) * ∫ z, G z ∂Γ := by
   211	  rw [← integral_map (measurable_const_smul r).aemeasurable hG.aestronglyMeasurable,
   212	    map_dilation hΓ hr, integral_smul_measure, smul_eq_mul,
   213	    ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (Real.rpow_nonneg hr.le _)]
   214	
   215	/-- Integrability against `Γ` transfers exactly under the dilation. -/
   216	theorem integrable_dilation_iff {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   217	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (G : Rd d → ℝ) (hG : Continuous G) :
   218	    Integrable (fun y => G (r • y)) Γ ↔ Integrable G Γ := by
   219	  have hm := (measurable_const_smul (M := ℝ) (α := Rd d) r).aemeasurable (μ := Γ)
   220	  show Integrable (G ∘ fun y => r • y) Γ ↔ _
   221	  rw [← integrable_map_measure hG.aestronglyMeasurable hm, map_dilation hΓ hr,
   222	    integrable_smul_measure]
   223	  · simpa using Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hr _
   224	  · exact ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top

   226	/-! ### Mean, variance, rate and integrated rate -/
   227	
   228	/-- The convolution `(Γ * φ)(x) = ∫ φ(x - y) Γ(dy)`. -/
   229	def conv (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (φ : Rd d → ℝ) (x : Rd d) : ℝ :=
   230	  ∫ y, φ (x - y) ∂Γ
   231	
   232	/-- `E:compact-raw-mean`: `h_{Ψ,s}(x) = ∫_0^1 |s-u|^{-a} (Γ * Ψ(u,·))(x) du`. -/
   233	def mean (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) (s : ℝ) (x : Rd d) : ℝ :=
   234	  ∫ u in Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, |s - u| ^ (-a) * conv Γ (fun y => Ψ (u, y)) x
   235	
   236	/-- `E:compact-raw-cost` in its integral form:
   237	`v_Ψ = ∫_0^1 ∫ Ψ(σ,x) h_{Ψ,σ}(x) dx dσ`. (Its identification with
   238	`E W(Ψ)²` is `L:compact-raw-profile`, not formalized here.) -/
   239	def rawCost (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   240	  ∫ σ in Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, ∫ x, Ψ (σ, x) * mean a Γ Ψ σ x

241	
   242	/-- `λ_{Ψ,s}` by `E:variational-real-rayleigh`:
   243	`λ_{Ψ,s} = √(sup{∫ h_s f² - ‖∇f‖₂² : f ∈ H^1(ℝ^d;ℝ), ‖f‖₂ = 1})`.
   244	(Its identification with `√(-E_s)` is `P:variational-unmasked-rate`, not
   245	formalized here.) -/
   246	def rate (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) (s : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   247	  WeakSobolev.rayleighRate (mean a Γ Ψ s)
   248	
   249	/-- `I_Ψ = ∫_0^1 λ_{Ψ,s} ds`. -/
   250	def integratedRate (a : ℝ) (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   251	  ∫ s in Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, rate a Γ Ψ s
   252	
   253	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the amplitude exponents,
   254	`r^{d+2-α} r^{α-d} = r²`. -/
   255	theorem amp_mul_push {alpha r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   256	    r ^ ((d : ℝ) + 2 - alpha) * r ^ (alpha - d) = r ^ 2 := by
   257	  rw [← Real.rpow_add hr, ← Real.rpow_natCast]
   258	  congr 1; push_cast; ring
   259	
   260	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `r^{d+2-α} r² (r^d)⁻¹ = r^{4-α}`. -/
   261	theorem amp_variance {alpha r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   262	    r ^ ((d : ℝ) + 2 - alpha) * r ^ 2 * (r ^ d)⁻¹ = r ^ (4 - alpha) := by
   263	  rw [← Real.rpow_natCast r 2, ← Real.rpow_natCast r d, ← Real.rpow_neg hr.le,
   264	    ← Real.rpow_add hr, ← Real.rpow_add hr]
   265	  congr 1; push_cast; ring
   266	
   267	/-- The convolution of a dilated control:
   268	`(Γ * D_rΨ(u,·))(x) = r² (Γ * Ψ(u,·))(r x)` (TeX lines 252-253). -/
   269	theorem conv_dil {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   270	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (u : ℝ) (x : Rd d) :
   271	    conv Γ (fun y => dil alpha r Ψ (u, y)) x = r ^ 2 * conv Γ (fun y => Ψ (u, y)) (r • x) := by
   272	  have hG : Continuous (fun z : Rd d => Ψ (u, r • x - z)) := by fun_prop
   273	  simp only [conv, dil, smul_sub]
   274	  rw [integral_const_mul, integral_dilation hΓ hr (fun z => Ψ (u, r • x - z)) hG,
   275	    ← mul_assoc, amp_mul_push hr]
   276	
   277	/-- Integrability of the convolution integrand transfers under `D_r`. -/
   278	theorem conv_dil_integrable_iff {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   279	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (u : ℝ) (x : Rd d) :
   280	    Integrable (fun y => dil alpha r Ψ (u, x - y)) Γ ↔
   281	      Integrable (fun y => Ψ (u, r • x - y)) Γ := by
   282	  have hG : Continuous (fun z : Rd d => Ψ (u, r • x - z)) := by fun_prop
   283	  simp only [dil, smul_sub]
   284	  rw [integrable_const_mul_iff (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hr _).ne'.isUnit]
   285	  exact integrable_dilation_iff hΓ hr _ hG
   286	
   287	/-- `h_{D_rΨ,s}(x) = r² h_{Ψ,s}(r x)` (`E:variational-dilation-values`). -/
   288	theorem mean_dil {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   289	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (a s : ℝ) (x : Rd d) :
   290	    mean a Γ (dil alpha r Ψ) s x = r ^ 2 * mean a Γ Ψ s (r • x) := by
   291	  simp only [mean, conv_dil hΓ hr hΨ]
   292	  rw [← integral_const_mul]
   293	  congr 1; funext u; ring
   294	
   295	/-- Integrability of the time integrand of the mean transfers under `D_r`. -/
   296	theorem mean_dil_integrable_iff {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   297	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (a s : ℝ) (x : Rd d) :
   298	    IntegrableOn (fun u => |s - u| ^ (-a) * conv Γ (fun y => dil alpha r Ψ (u, y)) x)
   299	        (Set.Ioo 0 1) ↔
   300	      IntegrableOn (fun u => |s - u| ^ (-a) * conv Γ (fun y => Ψ (u, y)) (r • x))
   301	        (Set.Ioo 0 1) := by
   302	  have e : (fun u => |s - u| ^ (-a) * conv Γ (fun y => dil alpha r Ψ (u, y)) x) =
   303	      fun u => r ^ 2 * (|s - u| ^ (-a) * conv Γ (fun y => Ψ (u, y)) (r • x)) := by
   304	    funext u; rw [conv_dil hΓ hr hΨ]; ring
   305	  rw [IntegrableOn, e, integrable_const_mul_iff (pow_pos hr 2).ne'.isUnit]
   306	  rfl

   308	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the spatial variance integrand of
   309	`D_rΨ` at time `σ`. -/
   310	theorem cost_integrand_dil {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   311	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (a σ : ℝ) (x : Rd d) :

   314	        ((r ^ d : ℝ) • (Ψ (σ, r • x) * mean a Γ Ψ σ (r • x))) := by
   315	  rw [mean_dil hΓ hr hΨ, smul_eq_mul, dil]

   319	theorem cost_inner_integrable_iff {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   320	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (a σ : ℝ) :

   328	`r^{4-α}`. -/

   343	  exact integral_const_mul _ _

   350	        (Set.Ioo 0 1) ↔

   356	260-264). -/
   357	theorem rayleighSet_mean_dil {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)

   366	theorem sSup_rayleighSet_mean_dil {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)}

   374	theorem rate_dil {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)

   382	theorem rate_integrable_iff {alpha : ℝ} {Γ : Measure (Rd d)} (hΓ : SetScaling alpha Γ)
   383	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ} (hΨ : Continuous Ψ) (a : ℝ) :

   403	  h.scaling

   405	/-- Lemma `L:variational-control-dilation` (TeX lines 225-237) with the
   406	section's standing hypotheses (line 4: a nonzero covariance satisfying

   411	and all fields of `H:homog` except the scaling are carried but unused. -/
   412	theorem variational_control_dilation_paper {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   413	    (hH : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (_hΓ0 : Γ ≠ 0) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   414	    Set.InvOn (dil alpha (1 / r)) (dil alpha r) (CPos d) (CPos d) ∧
   415	      Set.BijOn (dil (d := d) alpha r) (CPos d) (CPos d) ∧
   416	      ∀ Ψ ∈ CPos d,
   417	        (∀ s x, mean alpha0 Γ (dil alpha r Ψ) s x = r ^ 2 * mean alpha0 Γ Ψ s (r • x)) ∧
   418	        rawCost alpha0 Γ (dil alpha r Ψ) = r ^ (4 - alpha) * rawCost alpha0 Γ Ψ ∧
   419	        (∀ s, rate alpha0 Γ (dil alpha r Ψ) s = r * rate alpha0 Γ Ψ s) ∧
   420	        integratedRate alpha0 Γ (dil alpha r Ψ) = r * integratedRate alpha0 Γ Ψ := by
   421	  obtain ⟨hinv, hbij⟩ := dil_bijOn (d := d) alpha hr
   422	  refine ⟨hinv, hbij, fun Ψ hΨ => ?_⟩
   423	  have hc : Continuous Ψ := hΨ.1.continuous
   424	  have hS := setScaling_of_homog hH
   425	  exact ⟨mean_dil hS hr hc alpha0, rawCost_dil hS hr hc alpha0, rate_dil hS hr hc alpha0,
   426	    integratedRate_dil hS hr hc alpha0⟩
   427	
   428	/-- The integrability companion of `variational_control_dilation_paper`:
   429	under the same hypotheses, every integrand in the definitions of
   430	`h`, `v` and `I` is integrable for `D_rΨ` exactly when it is for `Ψ`, and
   431	the Rayleigh value sets scale (`R_{D_rΨ,s} = r² R_{Ψ,s}`), so nonemptiness and
   432	boundedness above hold for one side exactly when they hold for the other.
   433	This is a conditional transfer: it does not prove that either side is
   434	integrable, nonempty or bounded, so it does not by itself make the identities
   435	of `E:variational-dilation-values` identities of genuine integrals and
   436	suprema.  The integrability equivalences are Lean-route auxiliaries; the TeX
   437	proof states none of them. -/
   438	theorem variational_control_dilation_integrable_paper {alpha alpha0 : ℝ}
   439	    {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} (hH : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (_hΓ0 : Γ ≠ 0)
   440	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (Ψ : ℝ × Rd d → ℝ) (hΨ : Ψ ∈ CPos d) :
   441	    (∀ u x, Integrable (fun y => dil alpha r Ψ (u, x - y)) Γ ↔
   442	      Integrable (fun y => Ψ (u, r • x - y)) Γ) ∧
   443	    (∀ s x, IntegrableOn
   444	        (fun u => |s - u| ^ (-alpha0) * conv Γ (fun y => dil alpha r Ψ (u, y)) x)
   445	        (Set.Ioo 0 1) ↔
   446	      IntegrableOn (fun u => |s - u| ^ (-alpha0) * conv Γ (fun y => Ψ (u, y)) (r • x))
   447	        (Set.Ioo 0 1)) ∧
   448	    (∀ σ, Integrable
   449	        (fun x => dil alpha r Ψ (σ, x) * mean alpha0 Γ (dil alpha r Ψ) σ x) volume ↔
   450	      Integrable (fun x => Ψ (σ, x) * mean alpha0 Γ Ψ σ x) volume) ∧
   451	    (IntegrableOn
   452	        (fun σ => ∫ x, dil alpha r Ψ (σ, x) * mean alpha0 Γ (dil alpha r Ψ) σ x)
   453	        (Set.Ioo 0 1) ↔
   454	      IntegrableOn (fun σ => ∫ x, Ψ (σ, x) * mean alpha0 Γ Ψ σ x) (Set.Ioo 0 1)) ∧
   455	    (∀ s, WeakSobolev.rayleighSet (mean alpha0 Γ (dil alpha r Ψ) s) =
   456	      (r ^ 2) • WeakSobolev.rayleighSet (mean alpha0 Γ Ψ s)) ∧
   457	    (IntegrableOn (rate alpha0 Γ (dil alpha r Ψ)) (Set.Ioo 0 1) ↔
   458	      IntegrableOn (rate alpha0 Γ Ψ) (Set.Ioo 0 1)) := by
   459	  have hc : Continuous Ψ := hΨ.1.continuous
   460	  have hS := setScaling_of_homog hH
   461	  exact ⟨conv_dil_integrable_iff hS hr hc, mean_dil_integrable_iff hS hr hc alpha0,
   462	    cost_inner_integrable_iff hS hr hc alpha0, rawCost_integrable_iff hS hr hc alpha0,
   463	    rayleighSet_mean_dil hS hr hc alpha0, rate_integrable_iff hS hr hc alpha0⟩
   464

    62	/-! ### Test functions, weak gradients and `H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)` -/

    64	/-- `φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d; ℝ)`: smooth with compact support. -/
    65	def IsTestFunction (φ : Rd d → ℝ) : Prop :=
    66	  ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ

    68	/-- `g` is a weak gradient of `f`: for every test function `φ` and every
    69	direction `v`, `∫ f ∂_v φ = -∫ ⟪g, v⟫ φ`. -/
    70	def HasWeakGradient (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) : Prop :=
    71	  ∀ φ : Rd d → ℝ, IsTestFunction φ → ∀ v : Rd d,
    72	    ∫ x, f x * fderiv ℝ φ x v = -∫ x, inner ℝ (g x) v * φ x
    73	
    74	/-- The real Sobolev space `H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)`: `f ∈ L^2` with a weak gradient in
    75	`L^2`. -/
    76	def MemH1 (f : Rd d → ℝ) : Prop :=
    77	  MemLp f 2 volume ∧ ∃ g : Rd d → Rd d, MemLp g 2 volume ∧ HasWeakGradient f g
    78	
    79	/-- An `L^2` weak gradient is unique almost everywhere. -/
    80	theorem weakGradient_ae_unique {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g₁ g₂ : Rd d → Rd d}
    81	    (h₁ : HasWeakGradient f g₁) (h₂ : HasWeakGradient f g₂)
    82	    (hg₁ : MemLp g₁ 2 volume) (hg₂ : MemLp g₂ 2 volume) :
    83	    g₁ =ᵐ[volume] g₂ := by
    84	  have hloc : ∀ (g : Rd d → Rd d), MemLp g 2 volume → ∀ v : Rd d,
    85	      LocallyIntegrable (fun x => inner ℝ (g x) v) volume := by
    86	    intro g hg v
    87	    have : MemLp (fun x => inner ℝ (g x) v) 2 volume := by
    88	      have := (innerSL ℝ v).comp_memLp' hg
    89	      refine this.congr_norm ?_ (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_)
    90	      · exact hg.aestronglyMeasurable.inner_const
    91	      · simp [real_inner_comm]
    92	    exact this.locallyIntegrable (by norm_num)
    93	  have hcoord : ∀ v : Rd d, ∀ᵐ x ∂volume, inner ℝ (g₁ x - g₂ x) v = 0 := by
    94	    intro v
    95	    have hL : LocallyIntegrable (fun x => inner ℝ (g₁ x - g₂ x) v) volume := by
    96	      simp_rw [inner_sub_left]
    97	      exact (hloc g₁ hg₁ v).sub (hloc g₂ hg₂ v)
    98	    refine ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero hL ?_
    99	    intro φ hφ hφc
   100	    have i₁ : Integrable (fun x => φ x • inner ℝ (g₁ x) v) volume :=
   101	      (hloc g₁ hg₁ v).integrable_smul_left_of_hasCompactSupport hφ.continuous hφc
   102	    have i₂ : Integrable (fun x => φ x • inner ℝ (g₂ x) v) volume :=
   103	      (hloc g₂ hg₂ v).integrable_smul_left_of_hasCompactSupport hφ.continuous hφc
   104	    have e₁ := h₁ φ ⟨hφ, hφc⟩ v
   105	    have e₂ := h₂ φ ⟨hφ, hφc⟩ v
   106	    have : ∀ x, φ x • inner ℝ (g₁ x - g₂ x) v =
   107	        φ x • inner ℝ (g₁ x) v - φ x • inner ℝ (g₂ x) v := by
   108	      intro x; rw [inner_sub_left, smul_sub]
   109	    simp_rw [this]
   110	    rw [integral_sub i₁ i₂]
   111	    simp only [smul_eq_mul] at *
   112	    have c₁ : ∫ x, φ x * inner ℝ (g₁ x) v = ∫ x, inner ℝ (g₁ x) v * φ x := by
   113	      congr 1; funext x; ring
   114	    have c₂ : ∫ x, φ x * inner ℝ (g₂ x) v = ∫ x, inner ℝ (g₂ x) v * φ x := by
   115	      congr 1; funext x; ring
   116	    rw [c₁, c₂]

   118	  have hall : ∀ᵐ x ∂volume, ∀ i : Fin d,
   119	      inner ℝ (g₁ x - g₂ x) (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = 0 :=

   129	/-! ### The `L^2` dilation `U_r` -/
   130	
   131	/-- `U_r f(x) = r^{d/2} f(r x)` (TeX line 260), for real- or vector-valued `f`. -/
   132	def dilL2 {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   133	    (r : ℝ) (f : Rd d → E) : Rd d → E :=
   134	  fun x => r ^ ((d : ℝ) / 2) • f (r • x)
   135	
   136	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `(r^{d/2})² = r^d`. -/
   137	theorem rpow_half_sq {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) : (r ^ ((d : ℝ) / 2)) ^ 2 = r ^ d := by
   138	  rw [← Real.rpow_natCast (r ^ ((d : ℝ) / 2)) 2, ← Real.rpow_mul hr.le,
   139	    ← Real.rpow_natCast r d]
   140	  congr 1; push_cast; ring
   141	
   142	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: Lebesgue substitution `y = r x`,
   143	`∫ r^d G(r x) dx = ∫ G` (unconditional). -/
   144	theorem integral_jacobian {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   145	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (G : Rd d → E) :
   146	    ∫ x, (r ^ d : ℝ) • G (r • x) = ∫ y, G y := by
   147	  rw [integral_smul, Measure.integral_comp_smul_of_nonneg volume G r (hR := hr.le),
   148	    finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ (by positivity), one_smul]
   149	
   150	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: integrability is invariant under the
   151	substitution `y = r x`. -/
   152	theorem integrable_jacobian_iff {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   153	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (G : Rd d → E) :
   154	    Integrable (fun x => (r ^ d : ℝ) • G (r • x)) volume ↔ Integrable G volume := by
   155	  have e : (fun x => (r ^ d : ℝ) • G (r • x)) = (r ^ d : ℝ) • (fun x => G (r • x)) := rfl
   156	  rw [e, integrable_smul_iff (by positivity : (r ^ d : ℝ) ≠ 0),
   157	    integrable_comp_smul_iff volume G hr.ne']
   158	
   159	/-- `U_r` maps `L^2` into `L^2`. -/
   160	theorem memLp_dilL2 {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   161	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {f : Rd d → E} (hf : MemLp f 2 volume) :
   162	    MemLp (dilL2 r f) 2 volume := by
   163	  have hm : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => f (r • x)) volume :=
   164	    hf.aestronglyMeasurable.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving (Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_smul volume hr.ne')

   166	    rw [memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm hm]
   167	    rw [memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm hf.aestronglyMeasurable] at hf
   168	    exact (integrable_comp_smul_iff volume (fun y => ‖f y‖ ^ 2) hr.ne').mpr hf
   169	  exact this.const_smul _
   170	
   171	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: `‖U_r f(x)‖² = r^d ‖f(r x)‖²`. -/
   172	theorem norm_dilL2_sq {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   173	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (f : Rd d → E) (x : Rd d) :
   174	    ‖dilL2 r f x‖ ^ 2 = (r ^ d : ℝ) • ‖f (r • x)‖ ^ 2 := by
   175	  rw [dilL2, norm_smul, mul_pow, Real.norm_of_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hr.le _),

176	    rpow_half_sq hr, smul_eq_mul]

   178	/-- `U_r` preserves the `L^2` norm: `∫ ‖U_r f‖² = ∫ ‖f‖²`. -/
   179	theorem integral_norm_dilL2_sq {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   180	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (f : Rd d → E) :
   181	    ∫ x, ‖dilL2 r f x‖ ^ 2 = ∫ x, ‖f x‖ ^ 2 := by
   182	  simp_rw [norm_dilL2_sq hr]

   184	
   185	/-- `U_r` transports weak gradients: if `g` is a weak gradient of `f`, then
   186	`r U_r g` is a weak gradient of `U_r f` (TeX line 262,
   187	`‖∇U_r f‖₂² = r² ‖∇f‖₂²`). -/
   188	theorem hasWeakGradient_dilL2 {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d}

   201	        ((r ^ d : ℝ) • (f (r • x) * fderiv ℝ ψ (r • x) v)) := by
   202	    intro x
   203	    rw [hD, dilL2, smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul]

   205	  have hR : ∀ x, inner ℝ (r • dilL2 r g x) v * φ x =

   207	        ((r ^ d : ℝ) • (inner ℝ (g (r • x)) v * ψ (r • x))) := by
   208	    intro x
   209	    rw [hφψ, dilL2, real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_left, smul_eq_mul]
   210	    field_simp
   211	  simp_rw [hL, hR]
   212	  rw [integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul,
   213	    integral_jacobian hr (fun y => f y * fderiv ℝ ψ y v),
   214	    integral_jacobian hr (fun y => inner ℝ (g y) v * ψ y), h ψ hψ v]
   215	  ring
   216	
   217	/-! ### The real Rayleigh set of `E:variational-real-rayleigh` -/
   218	
   219	/-- A trial of the real Rayleigh supremum for the potential `V`: `f ∈ L^2`
   220	with `L^2` weak gradient `g` (so `f ∈ H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)`), `‖f‖₂ = 1`, and
   221	`V f²` integrable (explicit side condition, see the module doc). -/
   222	structure IsRayleighTrial (V : Rd d → ℝ) (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) : Prop where
   223	  memLp_f : MemLp f 2 volume
   224	  memLp_g : MemLp g 2 volume
   225	  weakGrad : HasWeakGradient f g
   226	  unit : ∫ x, f x ^ 2 = 1
   227	  integrable_pot : Integrable (fun x => V x * f x ^ 2) volume
   228	
   229	/-- The Rayleigh value `∫ V f² - ‖∇f‖₂²`. -/
   230	def rayleighValue (V : Rd d → ℝ) (f : Rd d → ℝ) (g : Rd d → Rd d) : ℝ :=
   231	  (∫ x, V x * f x ^ 2) - ∫ x, ‖g x‖ ^ 2
   232	
   233	/-- The set of real Rayleigh values over unit `f ∈ H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)`; its
   234	supremum is the right side of `E:variational-real-rayleigh`. -/
   235	def rayleighSet (V : Rd d → ℝ) : Set ℝ :=
   236	  {q | ∃ f g, IsRayleighTrial V f g ∧ rayleighValue V f g = q}
   237	
   238	/-- The rate attached to a potential: `√(sup of the real Rayleigh values)`.
   239	For `V = h_{Ψ,s}` this is the manuscript's `λ_{Ψ,s}` through
   240	`E:variational-real-rayleigh` (see `VariationalDilation`). -/
   241	def rayleighRate (V : Rd d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
   242	  Real.sqrt (sSup (rayleighSet V))
   243	
   244	/-- Every trial `f` lies in `H^1(ℝ^d; ℝ)`. -/
   245	theorem IsRayleighTrial.memH1 {V : Rd d → ℝ} {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d}
   246	    (h : IsRayleighTrial V f g) : MemH1 f :=
   247	  ⟨h.memLp_f, g, h.memLp_g, h.weakGrad⟩
   248	
   249	/-- The Rayleigh value of a trial depends only on `f` (uniqueness of the weak
   250	gradient), so the set over pairs is the set over `f ∈ H^1`. -/
   251	theorem rayleighValue_indep {V : Rd d → ℝ} {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g₁ g₂ : Rd d → Rd d}

   253	    rayleighValue V f g₁ = rayleighValue V f g₂ := by
   254	  have := weakGradient_ae_unique h₁.weakGrad h₂.weakGrad h₁.memLp_g h₂.memLp_g
   255	  unfold rayleighValue
   256	  congr 1
   257	  exact integral_congr_ae (this.mono fun x hx => by simp only [hx])

   260	`r² V(r ·)` with `r²` times the value. -/
   261	theorem IsRayleighTrial.dil {V : Rd d → ℝ} {f : Rd d → ℝ} {g : Rd d → Rd d}
   262	    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (h : IsRayleighTrial V f g) :
   263	    IsRayleighTrial (fun x => r ^ 2 * V (r • x)) (dilL2 r f) (fun x => r • dilL2 r g x) ∧
   264	      rayleighValue (fun x => r ^ 2 * V (r • x)) (dilL2 r f) (fun x => r • dilL2 r g x) =

   266	  have hpot : ∀ x, r ^ 2 * V (r • x) * dilL2 r f x ^ 2 =
   267	      r ^ 2 * ((r ^ d : ℝ) • (V (r • x) * f (r • x) ^ 2)) := by
   268	    intro x
   269	    have := norm_dilL2_sq hr f x
   270	    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs, sq_abs] at this
   271	    rw [this, smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul]; ring

   276	    intro x
   277	    have := norm_dilL2_sq hr f x
   278	    rwa [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs, sq_abs] at this

   282	  · simp_rw [hpot]
   283	    exact ((integrable_jacobian_iff hr (fun y => V y * f y ^ 2)).mpr
   284	      h.integrable_pot).const_mul _
   285	  · unfold rayleighValue
   286	    simp_rw [hpot, hgrad]
   287	    rw [integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul, integral_jacobian hr (fun y => V y * f y ^ 2),
   288	      integral_jacobian hr (fun y => ‖g y‖ ^ 2)]
   289	    ring

   291	/-- The real Rayleigh bijection (TeX lines 260-264):
   292	`rayleighSet (r² V(r ·)) = r² · rayleighSet V` for every real potential `V`
   293	and `r > 0`. -/
   294	theorem rayleighSet_dil (V : Rd d → ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   295	    rayleighSet (fun x => r ^ 2 * V (r • x)) = (r ^ 2) • rayleighSet V := by
   296	  ext q
   297	  constructor
   298	  · rintro ⟨F, G, hT, rfl⟩
   299	    have hri : 0 < r⁻¹ := inv_pos.mpr hr
   300	    obtain ⟨hT', hv'⟩ := hT.dil hri
   301	    have hV : (fun x => r⁻¹ ^ 2 * (r ^ 2 * V (r • r⁻¹ • x))) = V := by
   302	      funext x
   303	      rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_smul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_pow,
   304	        inv_mul_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_pow, one_mul]
   305	    rw [hV] at hT' hv'
   306	    refine Set.mem_smul_set.mpr ⟨_, ⟨_, _, hT', rfl⟩, ?_⟩
   307	    rw [hv', smul_eq_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_pow, mul_inv_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_pow, one_mul]
   308	  · rintro ⟨_, ⟨f, g, hT, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
   309	    obtain ⟨hT', hv'⟩ := hT.dil hr
   310	    exact ⟨_, _, hT', hv'⟩

   313	set `S` of reals and `r > 0` (no boundedness or nonemptiness needed). -/
   314	theorem sqrt_sSup_scale (S : Set ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   315	    Real.sqrt (sSup ((r ^ 2) • S)) = r * Real.sqrt (sSup S) := by
   316	  rw [Real.sSup_smul_of_nonneg (by positivity), smul_eq_mul, Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity),
   317	    Real.sqrt_sq hr.le]
   318	
   319	/-- The squared-rate identity: `sup R(r² V(r ·)) = r² sup R(V)`. -/
   320	theorem sSup_rayleighSet_dil (V : Rd d → ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   321	    sSup (rayleighSet (fun x => r ^ 2 * V (r • x))) = r ^ 2 * sSup (rayleighSet V) := by
   322	  rw [rayleighSet_dil V hr, Real.sSup_smul_of_nonneg (by positivity), smul_eq_mul]
   323

   325	theorem rayleighRate_dil (V : Rd d → ℝ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
   326	    rayleighRate (fun x => r ^ 2 * V (r • x)) = r * rayleighRate V := by
   327	  rw [rayleighRate, rayleighSet_dil V hr, sqrt_sSup_scale _ hr, rayleighRate]

    30	/-- Euclidean space `ℝ^d`. -/
    31	abbrev Rd (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
    32	
    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤
    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    39	  ν.map (fun x => -x) = ν
    40	
    41	/-- Positive-definiteness of `Γ` as a tempered distribution:
    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re
    48	
    49	/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention
    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:
    51	`∫ φ dΓ = ∫ (∫ φ(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx) μ(dξ)` for every Schwartz `φ`. -/
    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    53	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ
    56	
    57	/-- Hypothesis `H:homog`. Let `d ∈ {1,2,3}` and `0 < α₀ < 1`. The spatial
    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)
    81	
    82	/-- The numerical part of `H:homog`, in the form used by `DriverParameters`
    83	(with `a = α₀`). -/
    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    85	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    86	    DriverParameters.Homog d alpha alpha0 :=
    87	  ⟨h.dim, h.alpha0_pos, h.alpha0_lt_one, by linarith [h.threshold], h.alpha_range⟩

    89	/-- `E:kappa` with the manuscript's hypothesis: under `H:homog`,
    90	`κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α) ∈ (1, 2)`. -/
    91	theorem kappa_mem_Ioo_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    92	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    93	    KappaRange.kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 :=
    94	  KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo d alpha alpha0 h.dim h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one
    95	    h.threshold h.alpha_range

    97	/-- `E:driver-parameters` with the manuscript's hypothesis (the section
    98	retains `H:homog` and sets `a = α₀`): its strict intervals are nonempty. -/
    99	theorem parameters_nonempty_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   100	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
   101	    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
   102	      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - alpha0 / 2) ((3 - alpha0 - alpha) / 2)) :=
   103	  DriverParameters.parameters_nonempty d alpha alpha0 (homog_params h)

    21	\subsection{Global bounds and the unmasked spectral bottom}
    22	
    23	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian envelope for the original covariance]
    24	  \label{L:variational-heat-envelope}
    25	  For the normalized heat kernel $p_\epsilon(x) =
    26	  (2\pi\epsilon)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/(2\epsilon)}$,
    27	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-heat-envelope}
    28	    (\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    29	    =\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}\mu(\ud\xi),
    30	    \qquad
    31	    0\le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(x)
    32	    \le(\Gamma*p_\epsilon)(0)<\infty.
    33	  \end{equation}
    34	  The value at zero is strictly positive.
    35	\end{lemma}
    36	
    37	\begin{proof}
    38	  A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial ball growth. Indeed, evaluate
    39	  its tempered bound on a nonnegative smooth cutoff equal to one on $B_1$,
    40	  dilated by $R \ge 1$. Its finitely many Schwartz seminorms are bounded by
    41	  $CR^N$, so positivity gives a ball-mass bound $CR^N$. Summing dyadic annuli
    42	  shows that $(1+|x|)^{-L}$ is integrable for $L > N$. Apply this separately to
    43	  $\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Gaussian weights are therefore integrable against both
    44	  measures. The classical convolution on the left is finite and smooth locally
    45	  in $x$: on compact $x$ sets its translated Gaussian derivatives are bounded by
    46	  any fixed sufficiently fast polynomial weight in the integration variable.
    47	
    48	  Pair the convolution with a Schwartz test $\varphi$. Absolute Fubini is
    49	  justified by these weights. The resulting pairing is that of $\Gamma$ with
    50	  $p_\epsilon*\varphi$. Applying the spectral convention in
    51	  Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} and the identity $\int p_\epsilon(y)e^{-i\xi\cdot
    52	  y}\ud y = e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2/2}$ gives exactly the right side
    53	  of~\eqref{E:variational-heat-envelope} as a distribution. The heat kernel is
    54	  even, so either Fourier sign gives that same Gaussian multiplier. Its spectral
    55	  integral is absolutely finite and continuous in $x$ by dominated convergence.
    56	  Thus, equality of the two continuous distributions gives equality at every
    57	  $x$, without an extra normalization factor. The physical convolution is
    58	  nonnegative. Evenness of $\mu$ makes the spectral integral real, and its
    59	  absolute value is bounded by its total Gaussian mass, the value at zero.
    60	  Finally, $\Gamma \ne 0$ and $p_\epsilon > 0$ give strict positivity there.
    61	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope}.
    62	\end{proof}
    63	
    64	\begin{lemma}[Global regularity of the original mean]
    65	  \label{L:variational-global-mean}
    66	  Every mixed time and space derivative of $h_s$ is globally bounded in space,
    67	  uniformly on compact time intervals. In particular, for $I = [0,1]$ there are
    68	  finite constants $M,C_\Psi$ such that
    69	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-global-mean}
    70	    0\le h_s(x)\le M,\qquad
    71	    \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty\le C_\Psi|s-t|,
    72	    \qquad s,t\in I.
    73	  \end{equation}
    74	\end{lemma}
    75	
    76	\begin{proof}
    77	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time; its compact support inside $(0,1)$ makes this a
    78	  smooth extension. For any mixed derivative $D\Psi$, a fixed $\epsilon > 0$ and
    79	  compactness of its common spatial support give $|D\Psi(t,x)| \le
    80	  C_Dp_\epsilon(x)$ for all $t,x$. Here the heat kernel has a positive minimum
    81	  on that support. Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope} consequently bounds
    82	  $\Gamma*|D\Psi(t,\cdot)|$ uniformly in $t,x$. Ordinary local differentiation
    83	  against the Radon measure gives the corresponding derivatives of the
    84	  convolution. After the change $r = s-t$,
    85	  \[
    86	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
    87	    (\Gamma*\Psi(s-r,\cdot))(x)\ud r.
    88	  \]
    89	  For $s$ in a compact interval the relevant $r$ lie in a fixed bounded
    90	  interval. The preceding global bound times $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable since $a <
    91	  1$. Every derivative thus falls on the smooth test and passes through the
    92	  integral by dominated convergence, with the claimed global spatial bounds.
    93	  Nonnegativity follows from positive kernels. The bounded time derivative
    94	  proves the Lipschitz estimate. No directional decay of the mean has been
    95	  inferred. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-global-mean}.
    96	\end{proof}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   100	  On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   101	  $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
   102	  h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
   103	  positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
   104	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
   105	    \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
   106	    =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   107	    \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	  It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
   110	  positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
   111	\end{proposition}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  The Fourier Laplacian $A = -\Delta$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$, being
   115	  multiplication by $|\xi|^2$ with its maximal domain. Multiplication $B_s =
   116	  -h_s$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm at most $M$. Thus, $H_s = A+B_s$ is
   117	  densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are
   118	  equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,
   119	  \[
   120	    H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).
   121	  \]
   122	  The first factor has a Neumann inverse because $\|B_s(A-ib)^{-1}\| \le M/b <
   123	  1$, and the same holds with $+ib$. To check self-adjointness directly, for $u
   124	  \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
   125	  \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,
   126	  $D(H_s^*) = D(H_s)$.
   127	
   128	  Set $c_{\mathrm{shift}} = 1+M$ and $J_s = H_s+c_{\mathrm{shift}} \ge 1$.
   129	  Integration by parts on $H^2$ gives
   130	  \[
   131	    \|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2=q_s(f)+c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_2^2,\qquad
   132	    \|f\|_{H^1}^2\le\|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2
   133	    \le c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_{H^1}^2.
   134	  \]
   135	  Spectral cutoffs $1_{[1,n]}(J_s)$ show that $H^2 = D(J_s)$ is a core for the
   136	  half-power norm; Fourier cutoffs give its density in $H^1$. Completion in the
   137	  equivalent norms identifies $D(J_s^{1/2})$ and $H^1$ as $L^2$ subspaces, since
   138	  both norms dominate $L^2$. This proves the stated form domain.
   139	
   140	  The spectral lower bound gives one direction of the Rayleigh identity. For the
   141	  reverse, nonzero spectral projections in $[E_s,E_s+\epsilon]$ give unit $H^2$
   142	  vectors with Rayleigh values at most $E_s+\epsilon$. The bottom is finite
   143	  because the operator is bounded below and has finite Rayleigh tests. Let
   144	  $\epsilon\downarrow0$. Real tests give the same infimum: $q_s(u+iv) =
   145	  q_s(u)+q_s(v)$, so the quotient is the norm-weighted average of the nonzero
   146	  real quotients. This proves the Rayleigh identity with $-E_s$ on the left. The
   147	  following negative upper bound justifies writing that value as
   148	  $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2$ in~\eqref{E:variational-real-rayleigh}.
   149	
   150	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial} supplies, for this original
   151	  $\Psi$, one unit compactly supported $w$ and a finite plateau mask with a
   152	  common strictly negative upper bound $\epsilon_0 > 0$. Its trial has support
   153	  in $B_{2L}$; choose its plateau radius $R_0 \ge 2L$. The unmasked form on this
   154	  same $w$ is no larger. Consequently, $-M \le E_s \le -\epsilon_0 < 0$, and
   155	  $\sqrt{\epsilon_0} \le \lambda_{\Psi,s} \le \sqrt M$. Comparing identical unit
   156	  form tests gives $|E_s-E_t| \le \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty$ and therefore
   157	  \[
   158	    |\lambda_{\Psi,s}-\lambda_{\Psi,t}|
   159	    \le \frac{C_\Psi}{2\sqrt{\epsilon_0}}|s-t|.
   160	  \]
   161	  This also proves positivity and finiteness of $I_\Psi$. No compact-potential
   162	  spectral theorem was applied to $H_s$. This proves
   163	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate}.
   164	\end{proof}

   166	\subsection{Removing masks from the numerical lower rate}
   167	
   168	\begin{proposition}[Monotone rates and the original point moment]
   169	  \label{P:variational-remove-mask}
   170	  There is an increasing family of admissible radial masks $m_R$ tending to one,
   171	  for which the compact ground rates satisfy
   172	  $\lambda_{R,s}\uparrow\lambda_{\Psi,s}$ uniformly on $I$ as $R \to \infty$,
   173	  with the compact ground statements used for $R \ge R_0(\Psi)$. For the

   223	\subsection{Full-class dilation and finite variational values for nonnegative controls}
   224	
   225	\begin{lemma}[Radon and Rayleigh dilation]\label{L:variational-control-dilation}
   226	  For $r > 0$ the map
   227	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-control-dilation}
   228	    (D_r\Psi)(s,x)=r^{d+2-\alpha}\Psi(s,rx)
   229	  \end{equation}
   230	  is a bijection of $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$, with inverse $D_{1/r}$. With
   231	  the same original covariance,
   232	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-dilation-values}
   233	    h_{D_r\Psi,s}(x)=r^2h_{\Psi,s}(rx),\qquad
   234	    v_{D_r\Psi}=r^{4-\alpha}v_\Psi,\qquad
   235	    \lambda_{D_r\Psi,s}=r\lambda_{\Psi,s},\quad
   236	    I_{D_r\Psi}=rI_\Psi.
   237	  \end{equation}
   238	\end{lemma}
   239	
   240	\begin{proof}
   241	  Positive dilation preserves the full smooth positive nonzero class;
   242	  multiplication of its amplitude powers gives the stated inverse. Homogeneity
   243	  of the physical Radon measure gives, for every nonnegative measurable $G$,
   244	  \[
   245	    \int G(ry)\Gamma(\ud y)
   246	    =r^{\alpha-d}\int G(z)\Gamma(\ud z).
   247	  \]
   248	  Indeed, its left pushforward measure on a Borel set $A$ is $\Gamma(A/r) =
   249	  r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$. Positive Tonelli applies this identity inside the
   250	  temporal convolution, giving $h_{D_r\Psi,s}(x) = r^2h_{\Psi,s}(rx)$. Now use
   251	  the \emph{Lebesgue} substitution $z = rx$ in the original pairing:
   252	  \[
   253	    v_{D_r\Psi}=r^{d+2-\alpha}r^2r^{-d}v_\Psi
   254	    =r^{4-\alpha}v_\Psi.
   255	  \]
   256	  This distinguishes the Radon pushforward from the spatial volume factor; it
   257	  includes singular covariances and white noise.
   258	
   259	  The map $U_rf(x) = r^{d/2}f(rx)$ is a unitary bijection on real $L^2$,
   260	  preserving $H^1,H^2$ as sets under its inverse. Weak derivatives give
   261	  $\|\nabla U_rf\|_2^2 = r^2\|\nabla f\|_2^2$ and $\int h_{D_r\Psi,s}(U_rf)^2 =
   262	  r^2\int h_{\Psi,s}f^2$. The real Rayleigh bijection proves the squared rate
   263	  identity; the rates are positive, so their square roots and integrals give
   264	  \eqref{E:variational-dilation-values}. On $H^2$ this is also $H_{D_r\Psi,s}U_r
   265	  = r^2U_rH_{\Psi,s}$. Time has not been rescaled. For compact masks the
   266	  corresponding identity uses $m_R(rx) = m_{R/r}(x)$; a fixed mask radius is not
   267	  invariant. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation}.
   268	\end{proof}

   270	\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic variational lower bounds]
   271	  \label{P:variational-positive-scores}
   272	  For $c > 0$, the set of variational values
   273	  $\{cI_\Psi-v_\Psi/2:\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}\}$ is nonempty and
   274	  bounded above. Its finite real supremum $S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is positive and
   275	  satisfies
   276	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-homogeneity}
   277	    S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}=c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}},
   278	    \qquad
   279	    Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}},
   280	  \end{equation}
   281	  where $Q_2$ is the original point liminf. The coefficient-one value is an
   282	  auxiliary variational value; no first-moment or source-constant identification
   283	  is asserted.
   284	\end{proposition}
   285	
   286	\begin{proof}
   287	  Write $k = 3-\alpha > 0$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $m = q/k > 1$. Fix one
   288	  $\Psi_0$ from the nonempty class and put $I_0 = I_{\Psi_0} > 0$, $v_0 =
   289	  v_{\Psi_0} > 0$. Positivity of the latter is
   290	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}. For $r_0 = (I_0/v_0)^{1/k} > 0$, which need
   291	  not be less than one, the exact real-power identity gives
   292	  \[
   293	    I_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}-v_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}/2
   294	    =r_0I_0-r_0^qv_0/2=r_0I_0/2>0.
   295	  \]
   296	  This positive value is obtained from a smooth nonnegative control.
   297	
   298	  For $c > 0$ put $r_c = c^{1/k}$ and $K_c = c^m > 0$.
   299	  Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation} and the exact scalar powers give,
   300	  for every $\Psi$,
   301	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-set-scaling}
   302	    cI_{D_{r_c}\Psi}-v_{D_{r_c}\Psi}/2
   303	    =K_c(I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2).
   304	  \end{equation}
   305	  Since $D_{r_c}$ is a bijection of the entire class, the whole set of
   306	  variational values with coefficient $c$ is $K_c$ times the whole
   307	  coefficient-one set of variational values.
   308	
   309	  We prove boundedness before taking finite-real suprema. The independent
   310	  Theorem~\ref{T:full-upper}, for the \emph{same canonical solution}, gives
   311	  \[
   312	    \E|u(T,0)|^2\le e(T+2)^d e^{C_{\mathrm{up}}T^\kappa},
   313	    \qquad T\ge1,\quad C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty.
   314	  \]
   315	  Its prefactor is negligible: choose $\epsilon = \kappa/2 > 0$, use $\log T \le
   316	  (T^\epsilon-1)/\epsilon$ and $\log(T+2) \le \log T+\log3$ for $T \ge 1$, and
   317	  divide by $T^\kappa$. Thus, the original point limsup is at most
   318	  $C_{\mathrm{up}}$. One fixed test/mask lower bound gives a finite lower bound
   319	  for $Q_2$, so $Q_2$ is finite. By~\eqref{E:variational-unmasked-point-lower}
   320	  every coefficient-two variational expression is at most this same $Q_2 \le
   321	  C_{\mathrm{up}}$, uniformly in $\Psi$.
   322	  Equation~\eqref{E:variational-score-set-scaling} at $c = 2$ consequently
   323	  bounds all coefficient-one variational values by $C_{\mathrm{up}}/K_2$. The
   324	  nonempty set has a finite real supremum $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} > 0$ by the
   325	  positive test above.
   326	
   327	  For general $c$, set equality and $K_c > 0$ show that $K_cS_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   328	  is the supremum: it is an upper bound, and every smaller number is exceeded by
   329	  $K_c$ times a coefficient-one variational expression within the corresponding
   330	  positive distance of its supremum. This proves finiteness, positivity and the
   331	  first identity in~\eqref{E:variational-score-homogeneity}. Taking the
   332	  numerical supremum of the coefficient-two lower bounds proves the second.
   333	  Although $2^m > 2$, the resulting $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}} > 2S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   334	  is only a comparison of auxiliary variational values. It is not a Jensen
   335	  improvement without a first-moment identification. This proves
   336	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
   337	\end{proof}

   398	\begin{lemma}[The original mean and variance]\label{L:compact-raw-profile}
   399	  Let $\Gamma \ne 0$ satisfy Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, let $a = \alpha_0$, and
   400	  let real nonnegative nonzero $\Psi \in C_c^\infty((0,1)\times\R^d)$ be
   401	  arbitrary, without a separability assumption. Define
   402	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-raw-mean}
   403	    h_\sigma(x)=\int_0^1|\sigma-u|^{-a}
   404	    (\Gamma*\Psi(u,\cdot))(x)\ud u,\qquad
   405	    \overline{q}(x)=\int_0^1\Psi(u,x)\ud u,\qquad Z=W(\Psi).
   406	  \end{equation}
   407	  Then $h$ is smooth in time and space on compact sets, and
   408	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-raw-cost}
   409	    0<v_\Psi:=\E Z^2
   410	    =\int_0^1\int\Psi(\sigma,x)h_\sigma(x)\ud x\ud\sigma<\infty.

    24	\subsection{The common original noise and its exact Gaussian shift}
    25	
    26	Choose an integer $B \ge 1$, later fixed by the cone estimate, and take $0 <
    27	\delta < \min(1,1/B)$. Define
    28	\begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-clocks}
    29	  N=\left\lfloor\frac1{\delta B}\right\rfloor\ge1,\quad
    30	  s_m=m\delta B\ (0\le m\le N),\quad
    31	  \tau=\delta^{-1}-NB\in[0,B),\quad
    32	  g_\delta=\delta^{(1-a)/2}.

    34	For a smooth compact positive-fast-time test $f$, extended by zero, put
    35	\begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-pullback}
    36	  T_{\delta,m}f(s,x)

    43	\eqref{E:constant-phase-driver}, on the local horizon $[0,B]$, and set
    44	\begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-drivers}
    45	  X_m=g_\delta A_R(W_{\delta,m}),\qquad
    46	  H_m(u)=\int_0^uS_F(-r)iB_F(V_{s_m+\delta r})S_F(r)\ud r.

    51	\begin{lemma}[Coupled Gaussian block inputs]\label{L:raw-block-inputs}
    52	  Each $T_{\delta,m}$ is an isometry of the original test completion, respecting
    53	  covariance-null tests. All $W_{\delta,m}$ and $Z$ are on the same given noise
    54	  space, without an independence assertion. Let $\mathcal{K}(F)$ have the
    55	  operator norm and let $\mathscr{B}_0 = h_0^\theta([0,B];\mathcal{K}(F))$ be
    56	  the $C^\theta$ closure of zero-initial polygonal compact-operator paths. It is
    57	  a separable Banach space. In $\mathscr{B}_\delta = \mathscr{B}_0^{N+1}$ with
    58	  maximum norm, $(X,Z)$, $X = (X_m)_{m=0}^N$, is jointly centered Gaussian and
    59	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-covariance}
    60	    b:=\E[XZ]=\sqrt\delta\,H,\qquad H=(H_m)_{m=0}^N.
    61	  \end{equation}
    62	  Moreover,
    63	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-moments}
    64	    \|X_m\|_{L^p\mathscr{B}_0}
    65	    \le C_{R,B}\sqrt p\,g_\delta,\qquad p\ge1.
    66	  \end{equation}
    67	\end{lemma}
    68	
    69	\begin{proof}
    70	  Substituting $s = s_m+\delta u$, $t = s_m+\delta r$ in the original covariance
    71	  gives the factor $\delta^{a-2}\delta^2\delta^{-a} = 1$. Thus, the maps extend
    72	  isometrically through the null quotient. Direct test substitution gives
    73	  $W_{\delta,m}(f) = W_{\mathrm{fast}}(f(\cdot-mB,\cdot))$. These are explicit
    74	  common-space identities.
    75	
    76	  Finite-rank rational matrices in a countable real Hilbert basis are dense in
    77	  $\mathcal{K}(F)$: for compact $T$, $P_nTP_n \to T$ in norm by compactness of
    78	  $T,T^*$, and finite entries admit rational approximation. Polygonal paths with
    79	  rational breakpoints and such matrices give separability of $\mathscr{B}_0$.
    80	  To approximate breakpoints, use uniform convergence, uniform Lipschitz bounds
    81	  and $[f]_\theta \le (2\|f\|_\infty)^{1-\theta}\operatorname{Lip}(f)^\theta$.
    82	  The same inequality puts every zero-initial Lipschitz compact-valued path in
    83	  $\mathscr{B}_0$ by polygonal approximation. The finite original coefficient
    84	  paths $iA_jL_\psi$ have these properties. Their Gaussian sums converge in
    85	  $L^pC^\theta$ and hence in the closed space $\mathscr{B}_0$. Their laws and
    86	  the parent Gaussian norm bound give~\eqref{E:raw-block-moments}. Every finite
    87	  joint coefficient list with $Z$ is Gaussian on the same $W$. Scalar continuous
    88	  functionals pass through the $L^2$ limits, preserving Gaussianity by
    89	  convergence of variances and characteristic functions. Thus, $(X,Z)$ is the
    90	  asserted Banach Gaussian variable. Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\E\|XZ\| \le
    91	  \|X\|_2\sqrt v < \infty$, so its Bochner covariance exists.
    92	
    93	  The original covariance and the test pullback give
    94	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-mean-jacobian}
    95	    \E[W_{\delta,m}(f)Z]
    96	    =\delta^{a/2}\int f(u,x)h_{s_m+\delta u}(x)\ud x\ud u.
    97	  \end{equation}
    98	  Absolute Fubini uses compact supports, local Radon mass and $a < 1$. This
    99	  identity extends to the explicit matrix-element tests for the operator path on
   100	  $E$: their time indicator is approximated by smooth bounded tests on one
   101	  compact support, converging in the original covariance norm by dominated
   102	  convergence against $|u-r|^{-a}\Gamma$; their mean pairings converge as well.
   103	  The Sobolev adjoint is the one in~\eqref{E:driver-covariance-row}. Hence, the
   104	  path covariance is $g_\delta\delta^{a/2}H_m = \sqrt\delta\,H_m$ on real
   105	  Schwartz $E$ pairs. For constant inputs the two columns are the same $L_\psi$
   106	  inputs $(\psi,0)$ and $(0,\psi)$, and total finite propagation identifies
   107	  their deterministic response. The span of $E$ and both constant coordinates is
   108	  dense in $F$; $E$ alone is not. Boundedness, rational times and path
   109	  continuity prove~\eqref{E:raw-block-covariance} on all $F$. In particular, $H
   110	  = b/\sqrt\delta \in \mathscr{B}_\delta$. This proves
   111	  Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-inputs}.
   112	\end{proof}
   113	
   114	\begin{proposition}[Change of law on the whole norm-Borel space]
   115	  \label{P:raw-block-gaussian-law}
   116	  For every nonnegative norm-Borel $j$ on all of $\mathscr{B}_\delta$,
   117	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-gaussian-law}
   118	    \E j(X)=
   119	    \E\left[e^{-Z/\sqrt\delta-v/(2\delta)}j(X+H)\right].
   120	  \end{equation}
   121	  The equality is valid also as an extended nonnegative integral.
   122	\end{proposition}
   123	
   124	\begin{proof}
   125	  For real $s$, the density $e^{-sZ-s^2v/2}$ defines an equivalent probability
   126	  measure $Q_s$ by completing the square in the $N(0,v)$ density. For any finite
   127	  list $\ell$ of continuous real coordinates on $\mathscr{B}_\delta$, the
   128	  Gaussian vector $(\ell(X),Z)$ is equal in law to $(TG,z\cdot G)$ for a finite
   129	  standard Gaussian vector $G$. A positive covariance square root gives this
   130	  representation even when singular; no inverse is used. Here $Tz = \ell(b)$ and
   131	  $|z|^2 = v$. Substitution $G' = G+sz$ in its density gives
   132	  $\E_{Q_s}f(\ell(X+sb)) = \E f(\ell(X))$ for every bounded Borel $f$.
   133	
   134	  The matrix entries of each block in a real Hilbert basis at rational times,
   135	  together with $0,B$, generate the norm-Borel sigma-field. To see the
   136	  operator-norm point, for a countable dense set $\mathcal{D}$ of unit vectors
   137	  obtained from normalized rational finite basis combinations, $\|T\| =
   138	  \sup_{u,w\in\mathcal{D}}|\langle Tu,w\rangle|$. These pairings are finite
   139	  linear combinations of matrix entries. Supremum and H\"older norms of
   140	  continuous paths are suprema over rational times and pairs. Thus, distance to
   141	  every fixed element of $\mathscr{B}_\delta$ is coordinate-measurable. Open
   142	  balls are measurable by rational closed-ball approximation, and separability
   143	  makes every open set a countable union of balls from dense centers. Conversely
   144	  the coordinates are continuous. The cylinder sets form a generating pi-system;
   145	  uniqueness of probability measures extends the finite-coordinate equality to
   146	  all norm-Borel sets. Simple functions and monotone convergence give the
   147	  identity for nonnegative $j$. Finally, take $s = \delta^{-1/2}$ and use $sb =
   148	  H$ from~\eqref{E:raw-block-covariance}. The map and its deterministic
   149	  translate are defined on the entire input space; there is no translated
   150	  exceptional-domain assumption. This proves
   151	  Proposition~\ref{P:raw-block-gaussian-law}.
   152	\end{proof}

   154	\subsection{Small noisy blocks and a cone in the displacement-velocity space}
   155	
   156	For any $x \in \mathscr{B}_0$ define $D_x(u) = S_F(u)U_x(u,0)$ by the
   157	everywhere-defined linear Young map of
   158	Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear}. Write $D_m^0 = D_{X_m}$ and $D_m^+ =
   159	D_{X_m+H_m}$. The latter retains both the mean and the residual noise.
   160	
   161	\begin{lemma}[Uniform block error]\label{L:raw-block-uniform-error}
   162	  Let $M_\delta = \max_{m\le N}\|X_m\|_{\mathscr{B}_0}$, including its factor
   163	  $g_\delta$. Then $M_\delta \to 0$ in every finite $L^q$, and, for some $c >
   164	  0$,
   165	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-maximum-exponential}
   166	    \sup_\delta\E e^{cM_\delta^2}<\infty.
   167	  \end{equation}
   168	  With the deterministic $P_s$ in~\eqref{E:compact-F-block},
   169	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-operator-error}
   170	    E_{\mathrm{op},\delta}:=
   171	    \max_{m\le N}\sup_{0\le u\le B}
   172	    \|D_m^+(u)-P_{s_m}(u)\|_{\mathcal{B}(F)}
   173	    \longrightarrow0
   174	    \quad\hbox{in every finite }L^q.
   175	  \end{equation}
   176	\end{lemma}
   177	
   178	\begin{proof}
   179	  The maximum and~\eqref{E:raw-block-moments}, with $N+1 \le 2/\delta$, give
   180	  \[
   181	    \|M_\delta\|_p
   182	    \le (N+1)^{1/p}C\sqrt p\,g_\delta
   183	    \le C'\sqrt p\,\delta^{(1-a)/2-1/p}.
   184	  \]
   185	  For fixed $q$, choose $p > \max(q,2/(1-a))$ to prove the first limit. No
   186	  independence is needed. Choose an integer $n_0$ with $n_0(1-a) \ge 1$. For $n
   187	  \ge n_0$,
   188	  \[
   189	    \E M_\delta^{2n}
   190	    \le2C^{2n}(2n)^n\delta^{n(1-a)-1}
   191	    \le2C^{2n}(2n)^n.
   192	  \]
   193	  For $1 \le n < n_0$, Lyapunov bounds the moment by the appropriate power of
   194	  the $2n_0$ moment. These finitely many terms are bounded. For the remaining
   195	  exponential series, $n! \ge (n/e)^n$ gives a geometric tail $2\sum_{n\ge
   196	  n_0}(2ecC^2)^n$ for small $c$. This
   197	  proves~\eqref{E:raw-block-maximum-exponential}; no such assertion is made for
   198	  the unscaled maximum.
   199	
   200	  Let $H_m^{\mathrm{stat}}$ be the primitive for constant potential $V_{s_m}$.
   201	  Compact mea smoothness on $[0,2]$ and the statewise primitive bound give
   202	  \[
   203	    \sup_m\max(\|H_m\|_{C^\theta},
   204	    \|H_m^{\mathrm{stat}}\|_{C^\theta})\le H_0,\qquad
   205	    \sup_m\|H_m-H_m^{\mathrm{stat}}\|_{C^\theta}\le C\delta.
   206	  \]
   207	  Indeed, the potential difference is at most $C\delta B$ in $L^\infty$ and
   208	  $L^2$; integration of the bounded free groups gives its Lipschitz primitive
   209	  bound on this fixed horizon. On $\{M_\delta\le1\}$, local Young stability on
   210	  the fixed ball of radius $H_0+1$ gives $E_{\mathrm{op},\delta} \le
   211	  C(M_\delta+\delta)$. This proves convergence in probability. The global Young
   212	  bound also gives
   213	  \[
   214	    \max_m\sup_{u\le B}\|D_m^+(u)\|
   215	    \le C_B\exp\big(C_B(1+H_0+M_\delta)^{1/\theta}\big).
   216	  \]
   217	  Since $1/\theta < 2$, every finite power of this bound is dominated by a
   218	  constant times the exponential in~\eqref{E:raw-block-maximum-exponential}.
   219	  Uniform higher moments yield uniform integrability, proving
   220	  \eqref{E:raw-block-operator-error}. Suprema are measurable: on a countable
   221	  dense set of unit states each difference is continuous in $u$, so rational
   222	  times and those states suffice. Operator-norm continuity of the physical free
   223	  group is not used. Only $s_m \le 1$ supplies the ground templates. This proves
   224	  Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-uniform-error}.
   225	\end{proof}

   227	\begin{lemma}[Indexed cone and terminal displacement]
   228	  \label{L:raw-block-indexed-cone}
   229	  Fix $0 < \varrho < 1/2$. There are an integer $B \ge 1$ and positive
   230	  $\omega,\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}},c_*$ such that the following holds for every $N
   231	  \ge 1$. If $\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_N \in I$ have adjacent distances at most
   232	  $\omega$ and real bounded operator families $D_m(u)$, $0 \le u \le B$, satisfy
   233	  \[
   234	    \max_{m\le N}\sup_{0\le u\le B}
   235	    \|D_m(u)-P_{\sigma_m}(u)\|\le\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}},
   236	  \]
   237	  then, for $0 \le u \le B$,
   238	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-positive-product}
   239	    O_\phi D_N(u)D_{N-1}(B)\cdots D_0(B)e_0
   240	    \ge c_*(1-\varrho)^{N-1}
   241	    \exp\left(B\sum_{m<N}\lambda_{\sigma_m}
   242	    +u\lambda_{\sigma_N}\right)>0.
   243	  \end{equation}
   244	  No positivity, composition or independence assumption on the $D_m$ is
   245	  required.
   246	\end{lemma}
   247	
   248	\begin{proof}
   249	  From~\eqref{E:compact-normalized-complement} fix $C_{\mathrm{gap}} \ge 1$,
   250	  $\eta_{\mathrm{gap}} > 0$ so the normalized complementary norm is at most
   251	  $C_{\mathrm{gap}}e^{-\eta_{\mathrm{gap}}t}$. Define positive margins and
   252	  finite bounds
   253	  \[
   254	    a_*=\inf_I\ell_s(e_0),\quad j_*=\inf_I O_\phi(e_s),\quad
   255	    M_e=\max(1,\sup_I\|e_s\|),\quad
   256	    M_\ell=\max(1,\sup_I\|\ell_s\|).
   257	  \]
   258	  Also put $M_P = \max(1,\sup_I\|\Pi_s\|)$, $M_Q = 1+M_P$, $M_z = M_e+1$, $E_0 =
   259	  \|e_0\| = 1$ and $H_{\mathrm{obs}} = \max(1,\|O_\phi\|)$. Choose the aperture
   260	  \emph{first}: $\vartheta = \min(1,j_*/(16H_{\mathrm{obs}}C_{\mathrm{gap}})) >
   261	  0$. Next choose integer $B \ge 1$ with
   262	  \[
   263	    q_B:=C_{\mathrm{gap}}e^{-\eta_{\mathrm{gap}}B}
   264	    \le\min\left(\frac18,\frac{\vartheta a_*}{8M_QE_0}\right).
   265	  \]
   266	  Choose $\nu > 0$ such that $\nu M_z \le \min(\varrho/2,\vartheta,1/4)$.
   267	  Uniform continuity of $\ell_s,\Pi_s$ supplies $\omega > 0$ for which adjacent
   268	  distances at most $\omega$ give both norm differences at most $\nu$. Finally,
   269	  choose $\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}} > 0$ satisfying all five smallness conditions
   270	  \begin{align*}
   271	    M_\ell\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}M_z&\le\varrho/2,&
   272	    M_Q\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}M_z&\le\vartheta/4,\\
   273	    M_\ell\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}E_0&\le a_*/2,&
   274	    M_Q\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}E_0&\le\vartheta a_*/8,&
   275	    H_{\mathrm{obs}}\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}M_z&\le j_*/8.
   276	  \end{align*}
   277	  All denominators are positive. This order of choices uses the normalized
   278	  complement rather than a growing terminal norm.
   279	
   280	  The cone at $s$ consists of $z = Ae_s+r$, with $A = \ell_s(z) > 0$, $\ell_s(r)
   281	  = 0$ and $\|r\|_F \le \vartheta A$. In particular, $r = Q_sz$ and $\|z\| \le
   282	  M_zA$. For entrance, $z_1 = D_0(B)e_0$, with $b = \sigma_0$, has normalized
   283	  amplitude at least $a_*-M_\ell\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}E_0 \ge a_*/2$. Its
   284	  normalized residual is at most $q_BM_QE_0+M_Q\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}E_0 \le
   285	  \vartheta a_*/4$. Thus, it enters the cone with residual ratio at most
   286	  $\vartheta/2$ and amplitude at least $e^{\lambda_bB}a_*/2$.
   287	
   288	  For an old-cone state $z = Ae_b+r$ and an adjacent index $c$, rebase before
   289	  using the complementary estimate:
   290	  \[
   291	    \ell_c(z)\ge(1-\nu M_z)A,\qquad
   292	    \|Q_cz\|\le\|Q_bz\|+\|(\Pi_b-\Pi_c)z\|
   293	    \le(\vartheta+\nu M_z)A.
   294	  \]
   295	  For the next full block $D$ close to $P_c(B)$, put $x =
   296	  e^{-\lambda_cB}\ell_c(Dz)$ and $y = e^{-\lambda_cB}\|Q_cDz\|$. Since
   297	  $\lambda_c > 0$, the perturbation and smallness conditions give
   298	  \[
   299	    x\ge(1-\nu M_z-M_\ell\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}M_z)A
   300	    \ge(1-\varrho)A>A/2,
   301	  \]
   302	  and
   303	  \[
   304	    y\le
   305	    [q_B(\vartheta+\nu M_z)+M_Q\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}M_z]A
   306	    \le\vartheta A/2.
   307	  \]
   308	  The last inequality uses $q_B \le 1/8$, $0 \le \nu M_z \le \vartheta$ and
   309	  $M_Q\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}M_z \le \vartheta/4$. Together with $\varrho < 1/2$,
   310	  these give $y \le \vartheta x$. These are precisely the finite residual and
   311	  cone-conversion margins; the old residual was not assumed to lie in the new
   312	  kernel. Each full block therefore preserves the new cone and multiplies its
   313	  amplitude by at least $e^{\lambda_cB}(1-\varrho)$.
   314	
   315	  For the terminal $0 \le u \le B$, rebase once more to $c = \sigma_N$. The same
   316	  bounds give $\ell_c(z) \ge 3A/4$ and $\|Q_cz\| \le 2\vartheta A$.
   317	  Consequently,
   318	  \[
   319	    e^{-\lambda_cu}O_\phi(P_c(u)z)/A
   320	    \ge3j_*/4-2H_{\mathrm{obs}}C_{\mathrm{gap}}\vartheta.
   321	  \]
   322	  The perturbation changes this by at most
   323	  $H_{\mathrm{obs}}\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}M_z \le j_*/8$. Since
   324	  $16H_{\mathrm{obs}}C_{\mathrm{gap}}\vartheta \le j_*$, the result is at least
   325	  $j_*/2$. Combine entrance, all $N-1$ intermediate full blocks and this
   326	  terminal estimate to obtain~\eqref{E:raw-block-positive-product}, with $c_* =
   327	  a_*j_*/4$. The induction is empty for $N = 1$ and the estimate includes $u =
   328	  0$. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-indexed-cone}.
   329	\end{proof}
